report.summary: Dinner time in range improved after the previous carb ratio change. Breakfast meals still finish high, overnight corrections fall further than expected, and fasting nights show extra basal delivery.

findings.text: Breakfast: 5 of 6 comparable meals ended high, with a median rise of 3.1 mmol/L at four hours.
evidence: Comparable meals exclude overridden boluses and correction windows.
Five meals remained more than 2.0 mmol/L above their starting value at four hours.

findings.text: Overnight: three isolated corrections dropped glucose about 1.5 times further than the programmed correction factor predicts.
evidence: Correction nights are analysed separately from fasting basal windows.
Observed drops were 4.2 to 5.1 mmol/L; expected drops were 2.8 to 3.4 mmol/L.

findings.text: Overnight: on 4 of 5 fasting nights, delivered basal exceeded the programmed rate, with a median delivery of 128%.
evidence: Fasting windows exclude meals, corrections and exercise mode.
Hourly delivered-to-programmed ratios support this pattern; glucose drift alone is excluded.

findings.text: Lunch: three meals rose early and returned near their starting level by four hours. Review the recorded bolus timing alongside those meals.
evidence: Recorded boluses were at the meal time in the three matching windows.
The early rise alone does not establish its cause.

suggestions.text: Consider a breakfast carb ratio of 9.9 g/U, a 10% step from 11 g/U. Review the meal evidence with your diabetes team.
evidence: Five of six comparable breakfasts ended high.

suggestions.text: Consider an overnight correction factor of 3.08 mmol/L per U, a 10% step from 2.8. Review the isolated corrections before changing a setting.
evidence: Three isolated corrections fell about 1.5 times further than expected.

suggestions.text: Consider reviewing the overnight basal rate from 0.80 to 0.88 U/h, using the fasting delivery evidence with your diabetes team.
evidence: Four of five fasting nights required extra basal delivery.

watching.reason: The previous change helped. Continue collecting comparable dinners before another adjustment.
Review meal timing records alongside the early-rise pattern.
